Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book insights:

- Policy stance (FOMC 9/21/22): Hawkish. The target range was raised to 3–3.25% with guidance for ongoing hikes and continued balance-sheet runoff, tightening both short-end rates and liquidity/term premia.
- Credit conditions (SLOOS July 2022): Broad tightening in standards and terms across C&I, CRE, most mortgages, HELOCs, credit cards, and subprime auto; higher loan costs and collateral requirements. Demand stronger for C&I/HELOCs, weaker for CRE.
- Beige Book (August 2022): Overall activity was flat to modest across districts. New York noted elevated recession risk even as employment increased and tourism remained solid. Boston reported easing in materials prices such as steel, lumber, and copper, suggesting some relief in cost pressures. Across Federal Reserve Banks, lenders still reported demand for credit cards and commercial/industrial loans, even as standards tightened.
- Net take: Fed tightening plus bank-side tightening still skew growth risks to the downside. However, resilient labor markets and tourism, along with some input-price easing, temper the negativity and slightly improve disinflation prospects versus a SLOOS-only view.
